subject: United Kingdom
reviewer: Codex: separate same-agent evidence review; no independent human review claimed
review: Separate same-agent review after the full assessment: checked question wording and recorded agreement directions across all 15 axes, period and territorial scope, implemented arrangements versus proposals, counter-evidence, every inferred response and the source mapping. Corrected utility-ownership citations using current Commons and Scottish Government evidence; supplemented public finance and territorial consent evidence; removed an unsupported inherent-value interpretation of culture-nature-16. Reassessed authority-liberty-02 against the concurrently updated records wording before refreshing the actual bank hash. Immigration outcomes and Channel arrivals were not treated as legal permission or unrestricted settlement. Equality and plural identity were not assumed to imply open borders. Neutral answers on immigration, trade and causal traits describe mixed/conditional positions; causal claims not established by policy remain explicitly inferred. The constituent-nation analogy in assimilation-multiculturalism-06 and central-local-11 is limited, not proof of an Indigenous-specific policy. All 223 inferred answers are disclosed in the separate review JSON; 17 answers directly describe implemented arrangements. No independent reviewer or public-opinion calibration is claimed. Validation has no errors; neutral-count warnings reviewed and retained for substantive reasons. No compatible same-country-catalogue neighbour requires a similarity decision at this bank hash.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Competitive elections, opposition and judicial review coexist with Commons confidence, delegated decisions and parliamentary sovereignty. Petition thresholds lead to responses or debate, not citizen-triggered binding law.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Freedom House reports strong electoral rights but restrictions on protest. Judicial review of executive action is distinct from striking down sovereign primary legislation. Recall has statutory triggers; the UK is not a system of unrestricted public initiation.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Expression and association are protected, with material restrictions concerning protest, weapons, drugs, surveillance and search. PACE safeguards and warrant exceptions must be read literally.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Rights reports identify restrictive implementation, not just legal protections. ANPR routine retention is 90 days locally and 12 months nationally; reviewed evidential retention is an exception, not blanket multi-year retention of everyone. Bulk interception requires national-security necessity and oversight.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Equality protections, a plural national identity, recognised constituent cultures and religious dress accommodation coexist with English proficiency, shared civic obligations and participation. Private customs are not generally required to be replaced.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The cohesion document advocates both common identity and pluralism; future programmes are not proof of delivery. Equality duties require consideration of needs, not unlimited spending or a predetermined outcome. Multinational symbolism is only an analogy for the question about Indigenous peoples.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: The UK admits substantial lawful migration through work, family and protection routes, but requires permission and selective eligibility. New protection claims receive renewable temporary leave. Actual returns and border enforcement coexist with continuing irregular arrivals.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: ONS migration totals do not measure permanent settlement or an open-border entitlement. Channel arrivals are not equivalent to permission or asylum refusal; protection claims can succeed following irregular entry. No comprehensive annual settlement quota was identified; proposals are distinguished from commenced rules.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: The UK maintains deterrence, expeditionary forces and alliances while asserting legal constraints and diplomacy. Strategic capability is not evidence of unlimited willingness to use force.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The defence review sets future capacity aims as well as current commitments. Human involvement in AI weapons need not mean approval of each attack; deployment details remain uncertain. Treaty commitments and diplomacy temper military capability.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Parliament retains domestic legislative authority and the UK controls currency and admission, while participating in binding treaties, alliances and common trade rules.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Domestic enforceability and international obligation are different. ECHR membership is not a transfer of all legislative sovereignty; NATO cooperation is not a common foreign-policy federation. Brexit does not answer every international-cooperation item.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Private ownership dominates ordinary business, alongside public health provision, rail infrastructure, the BBC and strategic public investment. Regional utility ownership differs.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Public funding does not necessarily imply public ownership, and use of private contractors does not imply general privatisation. Planned water reform is not completed nationalisation; strategic public firms do not constitute general industrial ownership.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: An open trade orientation and negotiated barrier reduction coexist with tariffs, remedies, strategic industrial support and investment screening.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Free trade does not mean every product is tariff-free or all security restrictions disappear. Domestic subsidies and procurement social value are not automatically import barriers. Signed agreements are distinct from entry into force.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Market production, prices and private investment coexist with an industrial strategy, selective state investment, minimum wages and regulated essential services.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: An industrial strategy is not compulsory economy-wide production planning. Central-bank operational independence remains relevant. England’s rent reforms retain market-rent comparisons; devolved housing rules differ.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Progressive taxes, income-tested benefits and in-work support redistribute resources, with caps, conditionality and fiscal limits.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Redistributive institutions do not establish equal disposable incomes or benefit adequacy. Anti-poverty evidence identifies persistent hardship. Wealth-related taxes are distinct from a comprehensive annual net-wealth tax; no broad land redistribution was established.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Civil policy and law operate without a general religious veto, alongside established churches, Lords Spiritual, worship and faith-school arrangements.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Religion’s constitutional and ceremonial role differs across constituent nations. Civil recognition of religious marriages does not make religious tribunals sovereign family courts. Charity relief is generally a public-benefit framework rather than an extra religion-only exemption.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Same-sex marriage, diverse adoption eligibility and sex-equality protections coexist with inherited institutions and qualified school guidance.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Country-level social acceptance is inferred from institutional treatment, not population unanimity. The 2026 abortion assessment distinguishes existing clinical access, enacted provisions and commencement. Equality guidance differentiates sex and gender reassignment; neither blanket affirmation nor blanket exclusion is assumed.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: UK policy promotes AI, infrastructure and precision breeding while retaining medical, embryo and food safety controls.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Development priorities do not abolish environmental duties. The Nature Restoration Fund’s legal framework and delivery plans are distinguished. Precision-bred plants are not synonymous with all genetically modified crops, and regulated trials are not unrestricted consumer availability.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: The UK is a devolved parliamentary state: regional policy and some tax powers coexist with Westminster legislative sovereignty and national fiscal coordination.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Devolution is territorially asymmetric, and protected conventions do not equal an entrenched federal constitution. Northern Ireland’s consent principle differs from Scottish independence procedures. English administrative reorganisation proposals do not establish universal local self-determination.

axisReviews.evidenceSummary: Official education and health practice recognises learned development and biological influences; government genomics research expressly treats gene–environment interaction and context.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: These questions are especially interpretive for a state: policy intervention does not prove beliefs about majority causal shares. ADHD is not all normal attention, emotional regulation is not all temperament, and within-population heritability does not explain national or racial group gaps.

warningDecisions.decision: Five Neutral answers reflect conditional refugee protection, admission limits, services eligibility and settlement rules. Arrival counts are outcomes, not the position on each question.
Six Neutral answers reflect targeted security/strategic exceptions within a broadly trade-opening policy, not missing research.
Six Neutral answers reflect mixed gene/environment models; treatment evidence is not a quantified causal allocation or a population-wide belief.

limitations: Country profile describes institutions and implemented policy, not every resident.
223 responses translate contextual evidence into hypothetical or normative questionnaire language.
No independent human or separate-agent review; same-agent review is explicitly recorded.
Country identity questions have imperfect analogies; genetic evidence does not establish between-group causation.
